instructions:
# REST APIs

Hand-crafted skill for building and debugging REST APIs.

## What this skill does

- Models resources and picks the right verb per operation
- Exercises CRUD flows end-to-end with curl
- Reads and asserts on JSON responses with jq

## When to use

- Designing a new resource endpoint
- Reproducing a bug report against a running API
- Verifying behavior before writing tests

## Real commands

```bash
# Create (expect 201)
curl -s -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/orders -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"customer":7,"total":199}'

# Read one (expect 200)
curl -s https://api.example.com/v1/orders/7 | jq '.total'

# List with query params
curl -i https://api.example.com/v1/orders?page=2

# Full update vs partial update
curl -s -X PUT https://api.example.com/v1/orders/7 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"customer":7,"total":199,"status":"shipped"}'
curl -s -X PATCH https://api.example.com/v1/orders/7 -d '{"status":"canceled"}'

# Delete (expect 204)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X DELETE https://api.example.com/v1/orders/7

# Not found check
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://api.example.com/v1/orders/999
```

## Status code semantics

- 200 success, 201 created, 204 no content
- 400 client error, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found
- 409 conflict, 422 validation, 429 rate limited, 500 server error

## Testing

```bash
curl -s https://api.example.com/v1/orders | jq '.items | length'
```

## Best practices

- Use nouns for resources, not verbs: /orders not /getOrders
- Return 201 + Location header on create, 204 on delete
- Keep GET endpoints side-effect free
